questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My primary motivation for choosing my study destination was my personal connection with Japan through my heritage. Secondarily, I thought it was a unique opportunity to see first hand how the health care system works in a country that is very different from Denmark, as well as getting to rotate in 6 different departments, most of which I would have never visited during medical school otherwise.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was overall very happy with my experience, and I thought it was the perfect mix of study and exploring Japan. Of course it wasn't without its challenges, but most of it was expected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: No problems, my contacts at Tokai University were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I met with the university representatives for an orientation prior to my first day at the hospital, where I was informed about the program and showed around the hospital.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, as I couldn't secure accommodation before landing in Japan. Luckily I had planned to arrive a week before the program started, so I had time to figure it out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to live in the dorms provided by the university if possible. The off-campus housing was fine, but more expensive than the dorms. I only chose to do so because I came to Japan with my partner, and they couldn't accommodate them in the dorms.

questions.answer: Making plans outside of the programme with local students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit nearby cities (there are many popular and beautiful ones). To mention a few, Kamakura, Odawara, Hakone, Yokohama, Atari and of course Tokyo. And climbing mt Ooyama.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn't so difficult for me since I'm familiar with Japanese culture, but it might be fairly challenging if your'e not.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just start talking to them. They might be shy about talking in English since many of them don't think they're very good at it, but most can manage conversational English, and a lot of them want to talk to you but won't initiate the conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The intense hierarchy between doctors and students, the focus on memorization in their study technique.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness can be overwhelming when you're not used to it, but over time you grow to appreciate it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make the most of your free time, don't worry if you don't feel like you know as much as the Japanese students (they have a different way of studying), and try to learn some basic Japanese phrases and possibly medical vocabulary before coming (I found it very helpful).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to better understand experience the perspective of a medical student in a completely different health care system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language barrier
